questions.stem: Darwin observed that finches on different Galapagos islands had different beak shapes suited to different food sources. How does Darwin's theory explain this observation?

options.text: The finches deliberately changed their beak shapes to eat different foods
Individual finches with beak shapes better suited to available food survived and reproduced more, passing those traits to offspring over many generations
God created different finch species for each island
The finches' beaks changed during their lifetimes due to the type of food they ate

questions.explanation: Darwin's theory of natural selection explains that within the original finch population, there was natural variation in beak shape. On each island, finches with beaks better suited to the available food were more likely to survive and reproduce (survival of the fittest). Over many generations, this led to different beak shapes becoming dominant on different islands - an example of adaptive radiation.

questions.stem: Lamarck proposed that organisms can pass on characteristics acquired during their lifetime. A bodybuilder develops large muscles through training. According to modern biology, why would their children NOT automatically inherit large muscles?

options.text: Acquired characteristics are stored in the brain, not in DNA
Only changes to the DNA in gametes are inherited; muscle growth does not alter the DNA sequence in eggs or sperm
Children always look exactly like a mixture of both parents
The children's muscles would need the same exercise stimulus to develop

questions.explanation: Lamarck's theory of inheritance of acquired characteristics was disproven. Changes to the body during an organism's lifetime (like muscle growth from exercise) do not alter the DNA in the gametes. Only genetic information in eggs and sperm is passed to offspring. Weismann demonstrated this by cutting off mice tails for generations - offspring were always born with normal tails.

questions.stem: Fossils provide evidence for evolution. A scientist finds a series of horse fossils from different time periods, showing a gradual increase in body size and reduction from four toes to one. What does this fossil evidence demonstrate?

options.text: Horses were specially created in their modern form
Individual horses grew larger and lost toes during their lifetimes
Over millions of years, horse species gradually changed through evolution, with each generation slightly different from the last
Different horse species existed at the same time but were unrelated

questions.explanation: The fossil record shows a gradual transition in horse anatomy over approximately 55 million years. Each fossil in the sequence shows small changes from the previous one, providing strong evidence for gradual evolutionary change. This transitional series supports Darwin's theory that species change over time through accumulated small variations.

questions.stem: Darwin's theory was controversial when first published in 1859. Which of the following was NOT a reason for opposition at the time?

options.text: It conflicted with the religious belief that God created all species in their current form
Darwin could not explain how characteristics were inherited (genetics was not yet understood)
There was no evidence from DNA analysis to support the theory
Scientists at the time had already proven that evolution was impossible

questions.explanation: Options A, B, and C are all genuine reasons why Darwin's theory faced opposition. Religious beliefs conflicted with natural selection, and Darwin could not explain the mechanism of inheritance (Mendel's work on genetics was not widely known until 1900). DNA evidence was not available until the 20th century. However, scientists had NOT proven evolution impossible - many were simply cautious about the theory.

questions.stem: Alfred Russel Wallace independently developed a theory of evolution very similar to Darwin's. What was Wallace's key contribution that complemented Darwin's work?

options.text: Wallace proved that evolution was wrong
Wallace's observations of species distribution on islands supported the idea that geographic isolation drives speciation
Wallace discovered DNA and explained how traits are inherited
Wallace invented the microscope to study fossils

questions.explanation: Wallace independently developed a theory of natural selection based on his extensive work studying species in Southeast Asia. His observations of how species were distributed across islands (biogeography) provided strong supporting evidence for evolution. Wallace noted that closely related species were found in nearby but separate locations, supporting the idea that geographic isolation leads to the formation of new species.
